settings.ai.subagents: Let the AI use helpers to work in parallel
settings.ai.subagentsDesc: For jobs with several independent parts (reading many sites, comparing items), the AI can hand each part to a helper that runs at the same time and report back. Helpers only read pages and search the web, never click or type, and ask before visiting new sites just as the AI does. Also a button in the sidebar.
settings.ai.subagentModelDesc: Faster and cheaper is the default (for example Claude Haiku, GPT mini or Gemini Flash where your provider has one). Helpers’ tokens count in the chat’s usage.
settings.ai.autoUseDesc: Auto picks by task: quick chat and page questions go to a small, fast model, browsing to a reliable mid-size one, hard code and deep research to the strongest. Models out of usage are skipped. A model you pick is always used.
settings.ai.autoModel: Pick the model for me when I choose an engine’s Default
settings.ai.autoModelDesc: On Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build and Antigravity, Default picks per message: quick chat and one-step browsing use the small model (Haiku, Luna, Flash-Lite), multi-step browsing, research and code the mid-size one (Sonnet, Sol, Flash), hard debugging and proofs the strongest (Opus, Astra, Pro). A model you pick is always used.
settings.ai.autoFallback: Switch models automatically when one is unavailable
settings.ai.autoFallbackDesc: Continue with another model you’ve connected when yours is unavailable. The conversation may go to that provider. Off: you get the error and choose.
settings.ai.autoCompactDesc: When a chat nears the model’s limit, its earlier part is summarized instead of dropped. Your messages stay on screen. Type /compact to do it yourself.
settings.ai.cliFullAccess: Give all command-line AIs full access to this computer
settings.ai.cliFullAccessDesc: Sets all four together. Only turn this on if you trust them with your computer: a page they read could try to trick them. Half-way means only some are on. Off by default.
settings.ai.ccUserSettings: Use my Claude Code settings in Lumen chats
settings.ai.ccUserSettingsDesc: Off: Lumen’s Claude Code chats skip your CLAUDE.md, rules, memory and hooks, which saves tokens and startup time. Turn it on if you rely on them, or on proxy or environment settings in ~/.claude/settings.json. Full access always uses them.
settings.ai.claudeCodeFullAccess: Give Claude Code full access to this computer
settings.ai.claudeCodeFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Claude Code’s own tools.
settings.ai.grokBuildFullAccess: Give Grok Build full access to this computer
settings.ai.grokBuildFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Grok Build’s own tools.
settings.ai.antigravityFullAccess: Give Antigravity full access to this computer
settings.ai.antigravityFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Antigravity’s own tools.
settings.ai.codexFullAccess: Give Codex full access to this computer
settings.ai.codexFullAccessDesc: Runs commands and edits files without asking first, with its sandbox off. Lumen’s approval cards don’t cover Codex’s own tools.
settings.ai.grokTerminal: Let Grok Build ask to run terminal commands
settings.ai.grokTerminalDesc: Grok Build in the sidebar can ask to run a command on this computer, and runs it only if you approve. Off: it is told no every time, without asking you. Turning it off can also stop antivirus warnings about Grok’s chat logs.
settings.ai.grokWarmup: Warm up Grok Build when Lumen starts
settings.ai.grokWarmupDesc: Starts Grok Build’s setup in the background so your first message starts faster. Only while Grok Build is connected or chosen; nothing is sent to Grok.
settings.ai.grokKeepConnectedDesc: Each chat that uses Grok Build keeps its own Grok Build running between messages, so replies start sooner. Each one uses about 70 MB of memory while it waits. Messages with images, and Grok Build with full access, still start Grok Build each time.
settings.ai.codexKeepConnectedDesc: Each chat that uses Codex keeps its own Codex running between messages, so replies start sooner and stream as they are written. Each one uses about 80 MB of memory while it waits.
settings.ai.grokKeepIdle: Stop an idle Grok Build, Codex or Claude Code after
settings.ai.grokKeepIdleDesc: A kept Grok Build or Codex, or the Claude Code a chat keeps running between messages, that hasn’t been used this long is stopped; the chat’s next message starts it again. It also stops when its chat’s tab closes or the chat is deleted.
settings.ai.imageGenDesc: When you or the AI ask for a picture, Lumen sends the request to a provider you have already connected that makes pictures, even if the chat is on a model that can’t (Claude, Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex). Automatic tries the chat’s own provider first, then your other connected ones, and moves on if one is out of usage or down; a provider that refuses the picture on content grounds is not retried elsewhere. The picture says which provider made it. Your prompt goes to that provider, and it may count against its usage or your API key’s billing. Lumen never uses a provider you haven’t connected.
settings.ai.researchTabsDesc: Open pages the assistant searches or reads as background tabs in one group, loaded without your logins. Sites where AI is off are never opened.
settings.ai.maxStepsDesc: How many steps the assistant may take on one request before it wraps up. Unlimited still stops if it gets stuck in a loop, and Stop always works.
settings.ai.maxChatRunsDesc: Chats in different tabs can work at the same time. With a limit, once this many are working the next one waits its turn.

routines.template.email.description: Weekday mornings: what in your Gmail needs a reply.
routines.template.email.prompt: Check my email with the connector tool (app gmail, action unread). Summarize what needs a reply: who it is from, what they want and how urgent it is, most urgent first. Skip newsletters and automatic notifications and mention them in one line at the end. This is read only: never reply to, send, archive or delete anything. If the connector tool is not available, Gmail is not connected: say so and explain how to connect it (Settings, then AI and agents, then Connectors, then Gmail) instead of guessing.
routines.template.canvas.name: Canvas: what’s due today
routines.template.canvas.description: Weekday mornings: assignments due today and tomorrow.
routines.template.canvas.prompt: Use the connector tool (app canvas, action upcoming, days 2) to list what is due today and tomorrow, soonest first, with the course and the time. Add anything overdue and any announcement from the last day (action announcements, days 1). If nothing is due, say so in one line. This is read only. If the connector tool is not available, Canvas is not connected: say so and explain how to connect it (Settings, then AI and agents, then Connectors, then Canvas) instead of guessing.
routines.template.calendar.name: Weekly calendar preview
routines.template.calendar.description: Sunday evenings: what is on your calendar this week.
routines.template.calendar.prompt: Use the connector tool (app gcal, action events, days 7) to preview the week ahead: the events day by day with times and places. Point out clashes and the busiest days, and anything that needs preparing. This is read only. If the connector tool is not available, Google Calendar is not connected: say so and explain how to connect it (Settings, then AI and agents, then Connectors, then Google Calendar) instead of guessing.
routines.template.heartbeat.name: Heartbeat: inbox and calendar
routines.template.heartbeat.description: Every 30 minutes: tells you only if something needs you.
routines.template.heartbeat.prompt: Check whether anything needs me right now. Use the connector tool to read my unread email (app gmail, action unread) and, if Google Calendar is connected, my calendar for today (app gcal, action events, days 1). Something needs me when a real person asks me something or is waiting on me, when an email is time-sensitive, or when an event starts within the next hour or clashes with another. Newsletters, receipts and automatic notifications don’t count. If something needs me, say what in a few short lines, most urgent first. This is read only: never reply to, send, archive or delete anything. If the connector tool is not available, Gmail is not connected: say so and explain how to connect it (Settings, then AI and agents, then Connectors, then Gmail).

settings.gmail.step2: Press Enable on the Gmail API page.

Unread notifications work only with a classic token that has the notifications scope, because GitHub doesn’t offer notifications to fine-grained tokens; without one, the card shows the two lists and says so. Stored encrypted by your system; it never reaches the new-tab page and is sent only to api.github.com.
settings.widgets.github.showHelp: Lists are refreshed every few minutes. If GitHub’s rate limit is reached, Lumen waits until it resets.

settings.ai.bypassBackgroundDesc: With Bypass permissions on, background tasks and routines also stop asking: a new site, a signed-in account, and steps that buy, send, post or submit something are all answered Allow, with no one watching. A task is then no longer held to its allowed sites, and a page it reads could steer it. Each one is still listed in the task's steps. Without Bypass permissions this does nothing, and it switches itself off when you leave Bypass permissions. Off by default.
settings.ai.planModeDefault: Start new chats in plan mode
settings.ai.planModeDefaultDesc: A new chat starts with Plan on (the button next to the message box): the AI only reads pages, tabs and the web, then shows you a plan with the steps and the sites it will act on. Run plan carries it out and lets the AI click and type on those sites in that chat (opening or sending to them after reading a page still asks); Edit lets you change the steps first; Keep planning sends it back. Turn Plan off in the message box for one chat. Works with API models, not Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build or Antigravity. Off by default.
settings.ai.permissionModeDesc: Ask: the AI asks before it acts on a new site, reads a PDF, uses your signed-in account on a site, uploads a file or runs a tool or command. Auto-allow actions: it clicks and types on any site without asking, but still asks about the rest. Bypass permissions: every one of those questions is answered Allow for you, for the sidebar AI on every model and for connected agents, and the chat lists each one as a step (“Allowed automatically”). The AI won’t ask before acting, reading PDFs, using your signed-in accounts, or sending what it read anywhere, so a page it reads could steer it. Still in force: sites where you turned AI off, tabs you keep it off, Hands-off mode, and the rule that it uploads only files you attached or picked. The Choose file… card still waits for you, because Lumen can’t pick a file for you. The model is still told to stop before purchases and sending messages. Background tasks and routines bypass only if you also turn on “Bypass in background tasks and routines too”. Off by default.

settings.privacy.hideTab: Hide when you leave the tab
settings.privacy.hideTabDesc: Sites always see their tab as the one you’re looking at. They aren’t told when you switch tabs, switch to another app, put the window beside another in split screen or move the pointer off the page, so they can’t pause, nag or log you for it. Videos and games that pause when you look away keep playing. Applies to pages loaded after you change it.
settings.privacy.hideSizeDesc: Sites see a screen exactly the size of the window, so a window in split screen or made smaller looks like a full-screen one, and your screen size can’t be used to recognize you. Pages still fit the window. Applies to pages loaded after you change it.
settings.privacy.fingerprintDesc: Sites that can't use cookies try to recognize your computer by how it draws pictures, renders 3D and processes sound. Lumen changes those readings a tiny amount, differently on every site and every time you start Lumen, so they can't follow you from site to site. Nothing you see or hear changes. Your battery level is hidden too.
settings.privacy.webrtc: Hide your IP address from WebRTC
settings.privacy.webrtcDesc: Pages can use WebRTC, the technology behind video calls, to read your local network address, or your real address when a VPN doesn't cover all traffic. With this on they only get the address everyone already sees. Video calls still work.
settings.privacy.stripParamsDesc: Takes the parts of a link that only say where you clicked it (utm_ tags, fbclid, gclid, msclkid, mail-campaign ids, share ids) off the address before the page opens. The page you asked for still opens.
settings.privacy.pingsDesc: Stops the reports a page sends in the background when you click a link (link auditing) or leave it (beacons). Works while the ad blocker is on.
settings.ai.deviceAccess: Let the AI use files on this computer
settings.ai.deviceAccessDesc: The AI (and agents connected through the Automation server) can look in your folders, such as Desktop and Downloads, upload a file from them to a site you asked it to, and read the clipboard. The first upload to a site in a chat still asks unless you chose Auto-allow or Bypass. Lumen’s own profile, ssh, cloud and keychain folders and .env files stay out of reach.
settings.ai.stayOnMyTab: Bring tabs the AI opened to the front
settings.ai.stayOnMyTabDesc: On: the AI can bring a tab it opened to the front when it has a page to show you. Off: it keeps working in background tabs and never brings one to the front; the tab you are on stays in view.
settings.ai.closeAiTabsDesc: Leave open keeps them: a Close button under the reply, the tab menu and the chat list still close them. Ask puts the question under the reply. Close closes them when the AI is done, with Undo. A tab you clicked in, typed in, navigated, pinned or moved by hand is yours and stays, and so does the tab a chat lives in.

certError.heading: Your connection isn’t private
certError.lead: Someone may be trying to pretend to be {host} to steal your information, such as passwords, messages or card numbers.
certError.details: Lumen can’t confirm the certificate this site sent. It may be misconfigured, or someone may be intercepting your connection.
certError.reason.authorityInvalid: Its certificate isn’t issued by an authority this computer trusts (for example, it’s self-signed).
certError.reason.commonNameInvalid: Its certificate is for a different site, not {host}.
certError.reason.dateInvalid: Its certificate has expired or isn’t valid yet. Check that your computer’s clock is right.
certError.reason.revoked: Its certificate has been revoked by the authority that issued it.
certError.reason.weakSignature: Its certificate is signed with a weak algorithm.
certError.reason.weakKey: Its certificate uses a weak key.
certError.reason.nameConstraint: Its certificate was issued for names that its authority isn’t allowed to vouch for.
certError.reason.validityTooLong: Its certificate is valid for longer than browsers accept.
certError.reason.nonUniqueName: Its certificate is for a private name, not a public address like {host}.
certError.reason.noRevocation: Its certificate has no way to check whether it was revoked.
certError.reason.unableToCheckRevocation: Lumen couldn’t check whether its certificate was revoked.
certError.reason.transparency: Its certificate isn’t in the public logs that browsers require.
certError.reason.symantec: Its certificate comes from an authority that browsers no longer trust.
certError.reason.interception: Its certificate belongs to software that intercepts secure connections.

settings.unload.siteRejected: Not added: that is not a site, or it is already in the list.
settings.unload.noCurrentSite: No web page is open to add.
settings.unload.masterDesc: Closes the page of a background tab you have not used for a while to free its memory; it reloads when you come back. Turn off to keep every tab loaded.
settings.unload.afterDesc: How long a background tab can go unused before it unloads. Never turns the timer off: low memory, the limit below and your site list still apply.
settings.unload.howDesc: Unload closes the page and frees all its memory. Freeze keeps the page in memory, paused, so it wakes at once but frees less.
settings.unload.how.freeze: Freeze (keeps the page as it was)
settings.unload.freezeFirstDesc: An idle tab is frozen in memory for this long before it unloads, so coming back to it is instant. Costs some memory meanwhile.
settings.unload.capDesc: Beyond this many, the tabs unused longest unload (never one used in the last minute). Unlimited sets no cap.
settings.unload.keepRecent: Always keep the latest tabs loaded
settings.unload.keepRecentDesc: The tabs you used last are the ones you go back to, so the timer leaves them alone, and so does ordinary low memory (only very low memory, or your own GB limit, unloads them). The limit above can still unload them.
settings.unload.readyRecentDesc: Windows parks a tab you are not looking at in a low-power state, so the first moment after you come back can be slow. Lumen keeps this many of your latest tabs out of that state (and the tab under your pointer, always). Costs a little battery; on battery only one, and none when memory is low or the window is hidden.
settings.unload.readyNone: Only the tab under the pointer
settings.unload.pressure: Unload sooner when memory is low
settings.unload.pressureDesc: When free memory runs low, tabs unused for even a short time unload, oldest first. Low acts under 5% free (after 5 minutes unused), Medium under 10% (2 minutes), Aggressive under 20% (1 minute). On a Mac, Lumen follows the system’s own memory pressure.
settings.unload.lumenGb: Also when Lumen uses more than
settings.unload.lumenGbDesc: Counts all of Lumen’s tabs and processes. Needs a memory level above Off.
settings.unload.keepAudioDesc: A tab that is playing sound or video stays loaded.
settings.unload.keepForms: Tabs with unsaved input or a “Leave site?” prompt
settings.unload.keepFormsDesc: A tab with typed, unsent text, or a page that would ask “Leave site?” before closing, stays loaded.
settings.unload.keepCalls: Tabs in a call or sharing their screen
settings.unload.keepCallsDesc: A tab using the camera or microphone, or sharing the screen, always stays loaded, so a call or a share is never cut.
settings.unload.keepAgent: Tabs the AI agent or a background task is using
settings.unload.keepAgentDesc: These always stay loaded, so a task is never interrupted.
settings.unload.keepTransfers: Tabs with a download or upload in progress
settings.unload.keepTransfersDesc: A tab downloading a file, or with a file chosen to upload, stays loaded.
settings.unload.keepGroupsDesc: Tabs that belong to a group stay loaded. Off by default.
settings.unload.neverDesc: Tabs on these sites stay loaded. A name covers its subdomains; * works as a wildcard, for example *.example.com or mail.*.
settings.unload.neverNone: No sites. You can also right-click a tab and choose “Never unload this site”.
settings.unload.soonDesc: Tabs on these sites unload after their own, shorter time (below), even if they are among your latest tabs. The always-keep list wins over this one.
settings.unload.soonAfterDesc: Never longer than the usual time above.
settings.unload.dim: Dim unloaded tabs in the tab strip
settings.unload.dimDesc: An unloaded tab shows a dimmed icon and title, so you can tell it is not loaded.
settings.unload.showFreed: Show the memory freed when you hover an unloaded tab
settings.unload.showFreedDesc: The hover card adds an estimate such as “about 120 MB freed”. It is approximate: tabs of one site can share memory.
settings.unload.onReturn: When you switch to an unloaded tab
settings.unload.onReturnDesc: Reload the page at once, or show a page with a Reload button and load nothing until you press it. Hovering a tab does not load it in the second case.
settings.unload.restoreDesc: A reloaded tab gets its Back and Forward history back, and the browser restores the scroll position and form fields it saved for the page. Pages that rebuild themselves when they load, such as a document being edited, may start fresh, and text you had not submitted is why such tabs are kept loaded above.
settings.unload.preloadDesc: Once the first page has loaded and the computer is idle, Lumen loads the tabs next to it, one at a time, so they are ready when you click. Stops when memory is low, and is off while a Reload button is shown.
settings.unload.statusDesc: Tabs in all windows, updated while this page is open. Memory figures are approximate. Exempt tabs are loaded background tabs that would not unload now, because of the exceptions above or because they are a Lumen page.
settings.unload.perfAfter: Performance mode is on: tabs unload after {time}.
settings.unload.perfCap: Performance mode is on: at most {n} background tabs stay loaded.
settings.unload.resetDone: Page unloading settings are back to their defaults.
settings.unload.resetDesc: Puts every setting in this section back to its default. Your site lists are cleared too.
settings.ai.aiGapLog: Keep a list of what the AI couldn’t do
settings.ai.aiGapLogDesc: Notes, on this computer only, the times the AI still handed a task back to you after a second try: date, site, what was missing, the tool error. Never page content. See the list under Privacy below.

unloaded.lead: Lumen unloaded {host} to free memory. Nothing loads until you press Reload.

files.card.pinnedEmpty: Nothing pinned yet. Use + to pin a file or a folder.

widgets.files.desc: Shows the files and folders you pin and the ones you opened lately. Click one to open it. It stays on this computer; Lumen keeps only names and places, never what is inside.
settings.files.rememberDesc: Lumen remembers names and places of files you open, on this computer only. Never their contents.
settings.files.clearDesc: Forgets the recent files and the pinned ones. The files themselves are not touched.
settings.files.privacyRefDesc: Remember and clear them in General > Files.

settings.ai.hideAiTabsDesc: Leaves the tabs the AI opened out of the tab strip, in every window. They stay open; the one you are on and one playing sound stay shown. A tab that needs you (an approval, a dialog, an error) shows as "needs you" so it is never lost.

approval.app.always.title: Add this app to Settings → AI → Apps the AI can use. You can remove it there.
settings.ai.desktopControl: Let the AI use other apps on this computer
settings.ai.desktopControlDesc: Windows only for now. The AI can read and operate programs such as Word, File Explorer or MATLAB, one app at a time: it asks you before it uses each one, a banner at the top of the screen shows it working with a Stop button, holding Esc stops it, and touching the app yourself pauses it. It never reads or fills password fields, and Windows security prompts, password managers, banking apps and Lumen itself are never available.
settings.ai.desktopTerminalsDesc: Warning: a terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, Windows Terminal) can run anything on this computer, so only turn this on if you would let the AI type commands for you. Off by default.
settings.ai.desktopAppsDesc: Apps you chose Always for. The AI still asks about any other app, and you can revoke one here at any time.
settings.routines.title: Routines
settings.routines.desc: Requests the AI repeats on a schedule: switch them on or off, run one now, see what they did, and set quiet hours.
settings.routines.templates.desc: One click adds a routine that is switched off. Turn it on when you are ready.
settings.routines.webhooksDesc: Lets programs on this computer (Shortcuts, cron, a script, or a tunnel you set up) start a routine whose trigger is “From a web link”: a POST to 127.0.0.1 with that routine’s own key. It listens on this computer only, and each run still asks before it buys, sends or submits anything. Off by default.
settings.routines.webhookPortDesc: The local port the web links use (1024 to 65535).
settings.routines.webhookStatus.inUse: Port {port} is used by another program: pick another one.
settings.routines.failed: Couldn’t reach Lumen’s routines. Close this tab and open Settings again.
routines.quiet.title: Quiet hours
routines.quiet.on: No routine starts during quiet hours
routines.quiet.desc: A routine that is due during these hours waits and runs once when they end, marked as ran late.
routines.chat.request.placeholder: What should the AI do each time?
routines.chat.when.help: Say it in words: every weekday at 8am, every 3 hours, every Monday and Friday at 9am.
routines.chat.unreadable: I could not read that. Try “every weekday at 8am”, “every 3 hours” or “every Monday at 9am”.
routines.chat.error.request: Write what the routine should do.
routines.chat.saved: Routine saved. It runs in the background; see it in the sidebar’s Routines tab, on your home page and in Settings.
routines.card.emptyHint: A routine runs a request on a schedule and keeps what it finds.
routines.card.pausedHint: Switch them back on in Settings.
routines.card.offline: Offline: runs wait for the connection.

spotify.home.recommendedCaption: From Spotify, based on your top songs and artists.

spotify.home.moretopCaption: Top songs of artists you listen to, that are not in your saved songs yet.
spotify.home.genresCaption: Songs tagged “{title}”, a genre of your top artists.
spotify.home.genreartistsCaption: Artists tagged “{title}” that you do not follow.

spotify.library.failed: Couldn’t read this part of your library.
spotify.library.scope: Reconnect Spotify to show your library.

telegram.reply.stranger: This bot is linked to someone's Lumen browser and only answers its owner.
telegram.reply.paired: Paired. Send me a request and Lumen will work on it in the background. /help lists the commands.
telegram.reply.pairWrong: That code doesn't match. Check the code in Lumen's Settings and send /pair followed by it.
telegram.reply.pairLocked: Too many wrong codes. Press Pair in Lumen again to get a new code.
telegram.reply.forwarded: Forwarded messages aren't run: their words are someone else's. Type the request yourself if you want it.
telegram.reply.alreadyPaired: This chat is already paired with Lumen.
telegram.reply.textOnly: I can only take text requests for now.
telegram.reply.help:
Send a request and Lumen works on it as a background task, then sends the result here.
/status: what is running
/stop: stop the latest task
/help: this message
Lumen only works while it is open on your computer.
telegram.reply.unknownCommand: I don't know that command. /help lists the ones I do.
telegram.reply.alreadyAnswered: This question was already answered or has expired.
telegram.reply.deniedElsewhere: Denied (in Lumen, or nobody answered in time).
telegram.reply.stale: This message arrived while Lumen was closed, so it wasn't run. Send it again if you still want it.
telegram.card.head: Lumen needs your answer: {title}
telegram.card.interact: The AI wants to work on {host}.
telegram.card.wait: If nobody answers within {minutes} minutes, this step is denied.
telegram.state.badToken: Telegram didn't accept the bot token. Paste a new one from @BotFather.
telegram.error.tokenFormat: That doesn't look like a bot token. It looks like 123456789:AA… and comes from @BotFather.
telegram.error.noKeychain: OS encryption is unavailable, so Lumen can't store the token safely.
telegram.error.unreachable: Couldn't reach Telegram. Check your connection and try again.
telegram.error.unpairFirst: A chat is already paired. Press Unpair first, then Pair.
settings.telegram.pageDesc: Send requests to Lumen from your phone through your own Telegram bot.
settings.telegram.channel: Take requests from my Telegram bot
settings.telegram.channelDesc: While Lumen is open, messages you send to your bot run as background tasks and the results come back to the chat. Approval questions come to the chat with Allow and Deny buttons. Your messages and the results pass through Telegram's servers.
settings.telegram.signedIn: Use my sign-ins in these tasks
settings.telegram.signedInDesc: Same as “Use my sign-ins” on a background task: the task's tab uses your cookies. Off: it works signed out.
settings.telegram.tokenDesc: In Telegram, message @BotFather, send /newbot and paste the token it gives you. It is encrypted with your OS keychain and only sent to Telegram.
settings.telegram.pairingDesc: Only the chat you pair can use the bot. Messages from anyone else are ignored. To pair a different chat, press Unpair first.
settings.telegram.pairCode: Send /pair {code} to @{bot} in Telegram. The code works for 10 minutes.
settings.telegram.state.offline: Offline. Lumen will listen again when the connection is back.
settings.telegram.state.retrying: Couldn't reach Telegram. Trying again soon.
settings.telegram.state.conflict: Another program is reading this bot's messages (a webhook or another app). Lumen keeps trying.
settings.telegram.state.bad-token: Telegram didn't accept the bot token. Paste a new one.
dictation.start: Voice input: click to start and stop, or hold to talk ({key})
dictation.noMic: No microphone found. Connect one and try again.
dictation.micBlocked: Lumen can't use the microphone. Check that it is allowed for Lumen in your computer's privacy settings.
dictation.nothingHeard: No words were heard. Try again a little closer to the microphone.
dictation.off: Voice input is off. Turn it on in Settings → AI and agents → Voice input.
dictation.needKey: Voice input needs your {provider} API key. Add one in Settings → AI and agents.
dictation.needAnyKey: Voice input needs an API key from {providers}. Add one in Settings → AI and agents.
dictation.error.key: {provider} didn't accept the API key. Check it in Settings → AI and agents.
dictation.error.quota: {provider} says the key is over its limit or out of credit. Try again later.
dictation.error.tooLong: That recording is too long to turn into text. Keep it under two minutes.
dictation.error.audio: {provider} couldn't read the recording. Try again.
dictation.error.audioLocal: The recording couldn't be prepared ({detail}). Try again.
dictation.error.unavailable: {provider} isn't answering right now. Try again in a moment.
dictation.error.timeout: {provider} took too long to answer. Try again.
dictation.error.changed: The voice input setting changed while you were recording. Try again.
settings.ai.dictationProviderDesc: The mic button in the chat box records what you say and turns it into text with one of your own API keys. The recording is sent to that provider only, once, and is never saved. Automatic uses OpenAI, then Gemini: the first one with a key.
settings.ai.dictationAutoSendDesc: On: what you said is sent as soon as it is turned into text. Off: it goes into the chat box so you can read it over first.
shortcuts.dictate: Voice input in the chat box (hold to talk)
